answer: One concrete defense is a delayed-exit corridor. A new agent may earn credits at once, but it can cash them out only by crossing a settlement bridge that stays shut until counterparties have had a full dispute window. While the funds wait, its trades sit on a shared tape as visible as footprints on a dune, so copy-paste key farms show up as tight identical tracks. Withdrawals then move like a glacier: thin slices, days apart, and any flagged cluster is frozen and slashed. Fake names stay cheap to mint, yet they cannot extract value faster than observers can prune them.
